Release Notes

Michael Barkasi

November 01, 2026 (v2.6.0)

release_notes.Rmd

Planned changes for future releases

  • Experiment with extending the treatment knock-out (trtKO) functionality into a likelihood-ratio test for hypothesis testing. Update the tutorial on customizing statistical analyses, if needed.
  • Autodetect fixed-effect type, e.g., fixed-effect columns of R type “character” or “factor” are treated as two-level categorical factors, and numeric columns are treated as discrete additive effects (e.g., like a time series). Will need to update the RORB tutorial and any other tutorials which discuss time-series modeling.
  • Ensure any columns flagged as a time series are also treated as fixed-effects.
  • Add a check during the fit to see if any transition points can be replaced with a slope.
  • Add variable check to the loading of plot.settings in wisp. Currently only runs check_list without doing a more substantive check. Compare with the more detailed checks of MCMC.settings.
  • Allow MCMC.prior to be a vector of different prior distributions for each parameter. When completed, update the tutorial on customizing statistical analyses.
  • Ensure nested loops for matrix operations have the major axis (column) on outside.
  • Extracellular (out-of-soma) transcripts do not follow a Poisson distribution, and so any attempt to model them with wisp needs to account for this.

Version 2.6.1 (November 2, 2026)

  • plot.wisp’s type argument now defaults to “ratecount”, so plot(model) no longer requires naming a type.
  • Fixed plot.wisp silently ignoring the plot.settings a model was originally fit with when later re-plotting it: type = “ratecount” and type = “timeseries” now default their own log.scale, CI_style, dim.boundaries, count.alpha.ran/count.alpha.none, pred.alpha.ran/pred.alpha.none, and splitting_factor arguments to the model’s own plot.settings (as configured in the original wisp() call), rather than to a fixed value – matching how type = “species.summary” already behaved, and how every type’s cosmetic sizing/color settings already worked. These arguments can still be overridden on the plot() call itself. Note: a call that relied on the old behavior (a non-default plot.settings being ignored on manual re-plotting) will now see that setting applied by default; pass the argument explicitly to plot() to keep the old output.
  • Fixed analyze_residuals’s description, which had been copy-pasted from an unrelated internal helper (pvalues.samples) and incorrectly claimed the function computes p-values from an empirical CDF; it does not – it computes and summarizes raw/log residuals by group. Also expanded its documented return value with the group and plot-naming structure.
  • Expanded the wisp example, and the coef.wisp/confint.wisp documentation, to explain and demonstrate how to recover the original per-instance rate from a fitted Rt parameter (exponentiate, subtract one, divide by the mean number of data rows per bin – see the “Poisson processes and sigmoids” tutorial), and to distinguish it from the tslope/tpoint parameters (already on their natural scale) and the wfactor_rate/wfactor_slope/wfactor_point random-effect warping-factor parameters (present only when the random-effect factor has more than one level; a different kind of quantity from the like-named base parameters, not a rescaled version of one).
  • README.md is now generated from a new README.Rmd (via devtools::build_readme()), carrying the same self-updating “date (vX.Y)” build stamp as the other articles, instead of a hand-typed string that had already drifted out of date.
  • Fixed the peak-memory table under “Result 2” of the forking article, which was missing its 20-bootstraps/20-workers row – the data point the following paragraph’s “holding workers fixed at 20, doubling bootstraps from 20 to 40” comparison actually depends on.

Version 2.6.0 (October 29, 2026)

  • Breaking API change: the eight dotted plotting functions (plot.ratecount, plot.timeseries, plot.parameters, plot.effect.dist, plot.species.summary, plot.MCMC.walks, plot.decomposition, plot.MCMC.bs.comparison) have been removed. They looked like S3 methods but never were one, since wisp() used to return a plain, unclassed list, so plot() could never dispatch to them; users had to call each by its full dotted name. wisp() now classes its return value “wisp”, and all plotting goes through one real, exported S3 method, plot.wisp, selected with a type argument. All other arguments to each old function are unchanged and are simply passed through …. The old-name to new-call mapping is:
    • plot.ratecount(model, …) → plot(model, type = “ratecount”, …)
    • plot.timeseries(model, …) → plot(model, type = “timeseries”, …)
    • plot.parameters(model, …) → plot(model, type = “parameters”, …)
    • plot.effect.dist(model, …) → plot(model, type = “effect.dist”, …)
    • plot.species.summary(model, …) → plot(model, type = “species.summary”, …)
    • plot.MCMC.walks(model, …) → plot(model, type = “MCMC.walks”, …)
    • plot.decomposition(model, …) → plot(model, type = “decomposition”, …)
    • plot.MCMC.bs.comparison(model, …) → plot(model, type = “MCMC.bs.comparison”, …)
  • plot.wisp’s print.plots, verbose, and species arguments, previously only available by name on the underlying per-type functions (and so only reachable through …), are now named formals on plot.wisp itself: plot.wisp(x, type, print.plots = TRUE, verbose = TRUE, species = “all”, decompose = FALSE, …). Two of these are breaking changes:
    • print.plots now defaults to TRUE at the plot.wisp level (every underlying function’s own old default was FALSE). A call that relied on the old default to stay silent (e.g. in a script or non-interactive context) must now pass print.plots = FALSE explicitly to keep the old behavior.
    • species now defaults to the string “all” (translated internally to c()) rather than c() directly; this is purely a more readable public spelling of the same default and changes nothing about which species are plotted. species is only forwarded to type %in% c(“ratecount”, “timeseries”, “parameters”, “species.summary”) (the types whose underlying function actually has a species argument); passing a non-default species for any other type now raises a warning and is otherwise ignored, rather than erroring with “unused argument” or being silently (and confusingly) absorbed by ….
    • verbose defaults to TRUE, matching every underlying function’s own existing default, so this is not a behavior change.
  • Breaking API change: type = “decomposition” has been removed as a standalone plot.wisp type and folded into type = “ratecount” as a display mode, selected with a new decompose argument. plot(model, type = “decomposition”, species = “X”, …) becomes plot(model, type = “ratecount”, species = “X”, decompose = TRUE, …). As before, decompose = TRUE requires species to resolve to exactly one species level (not “all”, not a multi-element vector), or a clear error is raised; setting decompose = TRUE for any type other than “ratecount” is also an error. Unlike the old standalone type, the decomposed rate-count plots now honor the dispatcher’s shared print.plots and verbose arguments, just like every other type.
  • Added five new, real, dispatchable S3 methods for the “wisp” class, for the same reason plot.wisp was made a real S3 method in the breaking change above (plain exportPattern-based registration is not reliably found by dispatch once colorspace, a Depends: of this package, turns a base generic into an S4 generic for the session – so each of these also carries an explicit @method roxygen tag and an explicit S3method() NAMESPACE entry):
    • print.wisp(x, …): terse console digest of a fitted model (parameter count, grouping levels, resampling method/counts, and a stats summary).
    • summary.wisp(object, …) / print.summary.wisp(x, …): summary() returns an object of class “summary.wisp” wrapping objectstatsparameters plus model-size/fit-setting context; print() formats it for console display.
    • residuals.wisp(object, type = c(“raw”, “log”), …): returns the residual summary statistics (by group) computed during the fit, for either raw residuals or log-residuals.
    • coef.wisp(object, …): returns the fitted parameter estimates as a plain named numeric vector, per the usual R coef() convention.
    • confint.wisp(object, parm = NULL, level = 0.95, …): returns the already-computed confidence intervals (stored at whatever alpha was used when sample_stats last ran, default 95%) directly when level = 0.95; for any other level, transparently re-runs sample_stats (cheaply – it only re-quantiles the already-stored resampled parameters, without refitting) to recompute at the requested level.
    • All five give a clear, specific error (or message) rather than a cryptic one when called on a model fit with fit_only = TRUE (i.e. no statistical analysis was ever run).
  • Renamed the two exported warping/sigmoid math utilities wisp.warp and wisp.sigmoid to wisp_warp and wisp_sigmoid (dot to underscore). This is a pure rename with no change to arguments or behavior; it removes the last two function names in the package that looked like (but never were) S3 methods for a wisp generic (wisp() is the model-fitting function itself, not a generic, and never will be one).

Version 2.5.1 (October 3, 2026)

  • Updated .Rbuildignore.

Version 2.5 (October 3, 2026)

  • Improved time series parsing.
  • Updated time series plots to allow for tertiary effects.

Version 2.4 (July 3, 2026)

  • Part 2 of a major code refactor/optimization.
  • Finished refactoring wspc object class and its initialization method into a more organized structure.
  • Fixed issue in extrapolate_none.
  • Added option to level preprocessing coordinate transform (the cortical_coordinate_transform function) based on different layers.
  • Updated Roxygen2 descriptions for user-facing R functions.
  • Checked all tutorials to ensure they work with current version and removed auto-dating, so their current working version is properly documented. Included footnotes on saved and pre-processed code chunks.
  • Substantial code cleaning.

Version 2.3 (June 16, 2026)

  • Part 1 of a major code refactor/optimization.
  • Improved algorithm in check_parameter_feasibility for finding nearby feasible initial parameters.
  • Improved placement of check_parameter_feasibility within the various fit, MCMC, and bootstrap pipelines.
  • Converted several large-signature stand-alone functions into wspc methods: compute_gamma_dispersion, make_extrapolation_pool, find_count_log_means, estimate_change_points, and estimate_initial_parameters.
  • Simplified parameter vector handling.
  • Wrote checks into tutorials, to ensure code changes do not change results.
  • Replaced some R Lists with std::vector.
  • Improved weight-matrix construction.
  • Replaced pcg with std rng, to ease licensing issues.
  • Removed stan variables from wspc objects.
  • Replaced R-style masking with numeric indexing for summed count data.
  • Added print.settings argument splitting_factor_colors to wisp to allow users to specify colors for the splitting factor in ratecount and timeseries plots.
  • Performed extensive optimization of the code, leading to a x2 or x3 speedup in running wisp.
  • Documentation updated, but not yet rebuilt.

Version 2.2 (June 5, 2026)

  • Added model.settings argument max_bin to wisp which allows users to specify the largest bin number. If left at zero, the function will infer the maximum bin number from the count data.
  • Aligned matrix nested loops to major axis (column) to improve computational efficiency.
  • Updated plot.decomposition to allow for multiple contexts.
  • Fixed plot.timeseries to plot single-block species.
  • Added LRO parameter grid search option. (Very effective!)
  • Updated preprocessing functions for making count data.
  • Fixed batch size for forking.

Version 2.1 (March 1, 2026)

  • Added model.settings argument trtKO to wisp which enables excluding treatments to run reduced models.
  • Replaced corrupted data file “corticallaminar_model.rds” with working version (hopefully for the last time!).
  • Fixed memory leak related to CI computation.

Version 2.0 (Feb 19, 2026)

  • Release attached to NAR resubmission.
  • Redesigned plots.
  • Added attractor simulation functionality and benchmarking.
  • Includes first-draft versions of package tutorials.
  • Note that the package data file “corticallaminar_model.rds” was corrupted and should be pulled from the latest version or latest commit on the main branch.

Version 1.1

  • Added discrete time-series modeling functionality (the timeseries variable option) and plotting (the function plot.timeseries).
  • Ensured code would robustly run for any data including at least count and bin columns, without need for context, species, ran, or fixed-effect variables.
  • Added explicit fit_only option to wisp to avoid running any parameter estimation (MCMC or bootstrapping).

Version 1.0

  • Initial public release of wispack, as used in this preprint.
  • Defines the wisp function for implementing wisps.
  • Introduces one-dimensional warped sigmoidal Poisson-process mixed-effect modeling (one-dimensional wisps) for testing for functional spatial effects in spatial transcriptomics data.
